sources.entry: jumpstarter - A hardware-in-the-loop testing framework with a Python client library for automated testing on real and virtual hardware.

summary.one_liner: Jumpstarter is a free, open source test automation framework for running consistent automated tests on real and virtual hardware, with CI/CD integration and a programmatic (Python-first) interface.
summary.what_it_does: Jumpstarter provides a single toolset for testing both physical and virtual devices under test. It offers hardware abstraction through drivers for UART, CAN, SPI, GPIO, power, and USB. The Python client and `jmp` CLI integrate with PyTest and Python's testing ecosystem, so human developers, scripts, CI pipelines, and AI agents can use the same APIs. A Kubernetes-based Jumpstarter Service handles centralized hardware management, client and exporter routing, authentication, and multi-tenant use, and a gRPC/protobuf protocol layer supports tunneling over Unix sockets, TCP, and UDP. The README also describes sharing and securely leasing test hardware across teams.
use_cases: testing embedded devices in CI pipelines
running PyTest suites against real hardware
sharing and leasing test boards across a team
controlling UART, CAN, SPI, GPIO, and USB on devices
testing virtual and physical devices with one tool
notable: Monorepo with Python client/CLI, Kubernetes controller and operator, protocol definitions, and e2e tests
Same programmatic APIs for humans, test scripts, CI pipelines, and AI agents
Hardware drivers for UART, CAN, SPI, GPIO, power, and USB
Remote sharing and leasing of test hardware across teams
Tunneling over Unix sockets, TCP, and UDP with direct or routed topologies
caveats: Supports Linux and macOS only, according to the README
Deploying the Jumpstarter Service requires a Kubernetes cluster whose version must match controller/go.mod dependencies
Development requires Go, Python, and Docker/Podman plus kubectl
